findings.title: get_jit_options accepts valid-but-non-object JSON, silently discarding config and disabling caching for all bindings
findings.description: get_jit_options only guards json.JSONDecodeError; it does not assert that the parsed value is a dict. Valid JSON that is not an object (e.g. NUMBDUCK_JIT_OPTIONS='true', '5', '[1]', '"x"') passes json.loads and is returned as-is, so the module-level jit_options becomes a bool/int/list/str. Every wrapper in ducklib.py then calls @proxy(sig, jit_options=<non-dict>). numbox's proxy (proxy.py:69) coalesces this via `jit_options = isinstance(jit_options, dict) and jit_options or {}`, so a non-dict is silently replaced with {}. Because the empty dict omits cache, njit(sig)(func) at proxy.py:75 compiles with caching OFF for all 193 bindings, and the user's configuration is discarded with no diagnostic. This defeats the explicit intent of get_jit_options, which was written to reject bad config loudly (it raises ValueError for malformed JSON) but leaks valid-non-object JSON through.
findings.impact: A malformed-but-parseable NUMBDUCK_JIT_OPTIONS value silently disables the process-stable cached-compile path for every DuckDB binding (default is {"cache": True}) and swallows the misconfiguration instead of raising, making the failure hard to notice or diagnose. No wrong results, but a silent, whole-library performance/behavior regression that the intended ValueError guard was meant to prevent.
findings.recommendation: After json.loads, validate the type: `if not isinstance(as_json, dict): raise ValueError("NUMBDUCK_JIT_OPTIONS must be a JSON object")` (or equivalent), so both malformed and non-object config raise the same clean ValueError.
findings.failure_scenario: Set NUMBDUCK_JIT_OPTIONS='true' (or '5'), import numbduck.ducklib: get_jit_options returns True; jit_options=True; every @proxy coalesces to {}; all 193 bindings compile with cache disabled and the config is silently ignored, with no error raised.

notes: Mechanical migration is clean and complete. Verified: 193 registered signatures (ducklib.py:78-273) map 1:1 to 193 decorated wrappers to 193 _call_lib_func/_call_lib_func_byval call keys, all three strings matching per function (no wrong signature key, no lost decorator, no duplicate). 190 plain @proxy + 3 @proxy_if_available; every plain @proxy passes jit_options=jit_options; every @proxy_if_available passes duckdb_lib as its first positional arg then signatures.get(key) then jit_options=jit_options (lines 726 duckdb_create_varint, 1051 duckdb_get_varint, 1285 duckdb_scalar_function_set_init). No signatures.get(...) returns None (all keys are registered). jit_options is the shared module-level dict from configurations.py; numbox's proxy .copy()s it per call (proxy.py:70) so there is no cross-wrapper mutation, and the cache=True default composes correctly with the process-stable cfunc-alias mechanism (proxy.py:_stable_cfunc_alias / add_symbol) — no defect. Struct-by-value wrappers (duckdb_fetch_chunk:943, duckdb_result_return_type:1129, duckdb_result_statement_type:1135) use _call_lib_func_byval in the body; @proxy forwards numba-typed args to the body's cfunc wrapper via get_data_type-matched first-class aggregates, so large-tuple-by-value args are handled the same as any other signature (no ABI mismatch introduced by the swap). UNVERIFIED (no duckdb.h on disk, no duckdb installed): whether the gated set {duckdb_create_varint, duckdb_get_varint, duckdb_scalar_function_set_init} is EXACTLY the set of symbols absent in the minimum-pinned duckdb 1.3.2. Because a plain @proxy on a symbol missing from the loaded lib aborts module import (proxy eagerly compiles + get_pointer_to_function finalizes the cfunc wrapper), any post-1.3.2 symbol left on plain @proxy is a latent import-time crash on the floor version. In particular duckdb_scalar_function_set_bind (line 1255, plain @proxy) belongs to the same scalar-function bind/init extension family as the gated duckdb_scalar_function_set_init (line 1285); if both were added in the same duckdb release, the gating is inconsistent. This should be verified against duckdb.h for v1.3.2 / v1.4 / v1.5 before shipping — flagged here as a verification gap, not asserted as a confirmed defect.
